task: Regression: when `gnu` is False, `humanize.naturalsize(1.0)` or `naturalsize("1")` returns `"1.0 Byte"` instead of `"1 Byte"`, which was the return value until 4.12. Restore the previous output for float and numeric-string inputs that are below one kilobyte.
why:
The source fix is identical in every candidate, so the pick came down to test fit and minimality (maintainability). c4 puts its tests next to the existing `[1, False, False] -> "1 Byte"` case. It covers the reported inputs (`1.0`, `"1"`) plus the numeric string `"1.0"` and gnu-mode `1.0 -> "1B"`, so the fix is shown to leave the gnu path alone.
Runner-up c1 is the same fix with tests for only the two literal inputs from the report; it lost because it checks neither `"1.0"` nor the gnu path.
c2 and c3 add `300.0`/`"300"` cases, which were never broken. c3 also re-adds `[1]`, which the existing `[1, False, False]` case already covers.
